reason: The text depicts Hebrew leaders (Nehemiah and the officials/priests) as supportive of the Hebrew people's restoration efforts. Nehemiah galvanizes the people to rebuild Jerusalem's walls with the encouragement 'Let us rise up and build,' and the people respond positively ('they strengthened their hands for this good work'). The antagonism shown in the passage comes from foreign leaders—Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite slave, and Geshem the Arab—who 'laughed [them] to scorn, and despised [them],' not from Hebrew leaders.
